code: released_rates <- function(table, group, year) {   days <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean(paste0(table, "$risk_days"),     type = "combine", datasources = conns)$Global.Mean   py <- days[1, "EstimatedMean"] * days[1, "Nvalid"] / 365.25   do.call(rbind, lapply(c(mi = "Myocardial infarction", pneumonia = "Pneumonia"), function(cause) {     variable <- if (cause == "Pneumonia") "pneumonia" else "mi"     x <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean(paste0(table, "$", variable),       type = "combine", datasources = conns)$Global.Mean     stopifnot(x[1, "Nvalid"] == days[1, "Nvalid"], x[1, "Nmissing"] == 0,       days[1, "Nmissing"] == 0)     deaths <- round(x[1, "EstimatedMean"] * x[1, "Nvalid"])     ci <- stats::poisson.test(deaths, T = py)$conf.int * 1000     data.frame(Year = year, Group = group, Cause = cause, People = days[1, "Nvalid"],       Deaths = deaths, Person_years = py, Rate_per_1000 = 1000 * deaths / py,       Lower_95 = ci[1], Upper_95 = ci[2])   })) } rates_2024 <- released_rates("D_risk_2024", "All", 2024) rates_2024

Northern seasons Winter, Spring, Summer, Autumn (December-February first); southern names Summer, Autumn, Winter, Spring. Cyclic values use 2*pi*(k-1)/P P=12, 7 4. Custom patterns accept %Y, %m, %d, %j, %G, %V, %u, %b, %B, %, %, %% ASCII letters, digits, space -_/.,:(). ISO %G %V must appear together without %Y. locale, code time--day directives evaluated. code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ recipe <- omop_recipe(   blocks = omop_variable_block(     table = "condition_occurrence",     concept_ids = c(201820),     format = "binary"   ),   variables = list(     omop_variable_age(),     omop_variable(table = "measurement", concept_id = 3004410,                   format = "mean")   ),   filters = omop_filter_sex("F"),   outputs = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide") ) recipe_execute(recipe)  # Multi-population: build two criteria subgroups, UNION them into one # population, then run an output against that union while a recipe-level # scope (a cohort handle INTERSECTED with a workspace omop.table's persons) # narrows every population. recipe2 <- omop_recipe(   populations = list(     omop_population("diabetic", "Diabetics",                     filters = list(omop_filter_has_concept(                       201820, "condition_occurrence"))),     omop_population("hypertensive", "Hypertensives",                     filters = list(omop_filter_has_concept(                       320128, "condition_occurrence"))),     omop_population("either", "Diabetic or hypertensive",                     union = c("diabetic", "hypertensive"))   ),   variables = omop_variable_age(),   outputs = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide",                         population_id = "either"),   cohort = my_cohort_handle,   # cohort handle / table name as scope   tables = "my_inclusion_set", # workspace omop.table symbol name   combine = "intersect" ) recipe_execute(recipe2)  # `cohort=` is ALWAYS scope, including a bare cohort_definition_id: it resolves # to a gated person set that narrows every population. To instead BUILD the base # population from an existing admin/ATLAS cohort, pass it through # omop_population(cohort_definition_id = ...); `cohort=` then layers a scope on # top. recipe3 <- omop_recipe(   populations = omop_population(id = "base", label = "Registry cohort",                                 cohort_definition_id = 1001),  # base population   variables = omop_variable_age(),   outputs = omop_output(name = "study", type = "wide"),   cohort = 2002                                               # scalar id = scope ) recipe_execute(recipe3) } # }

title: A study in one call (simple layer) — omop_study
text: omop_study() returns ordinary omop_recipe: one indexed population (id name) requested outputs . exactly advanced recipe (recipe_to_code() prints ; print() lists every default study chose): population: omop_population(name, index = omop_index(index,     select = select), filters = <require>, coverage = coverage);     index omop_population (e.g.     omop_new_users) omop_index, index     criteria kept requirements ANDed . require: prior_observation = n     omop_observed(= n), followup = n     omop_observed(= n), age = c(min, max)     omop_age_is(min, max) (NA = open), sex = "F" /     "M" omop_person(omop_where(gender_concept_id == 8532))     (8507), = list(<events>) omop_has(e, window =     omop_window(NULL, 0)) (time index date),     no_history_of = list(<events>) omop_has_not(e, window     = omop_window(NULL, -1)) (time index date),     in_cohort = id omop_in_cohort(id); criterion objects     used ; order given. "baseline": wide output episode grain     every baseline variable (nested lists omop_history()     spliced ). "survival": survival output (competing_risk     two outcomes) tar = omop_window(start, end)     censor list follow_up. "long": long output outcome events     sources (relative dates). "panel": dense person_period output 30-day bins     follow-window, counting outcomes. simple layer never exposes grain, ties date handling: every output episode grain, survival ties use priority rule dates relative index; recipe_explain() states . "survival", "long" "panel" output without outcomes, "baseline" output without baseline variables, structural error.
